The api went down because the disk filled up: the `report-export` job filled `/var/lib/stockroom`, the database could no longer write, and the api exited at 03:14:06 on 2026-03-09. It was still down when the log ends at 05:29:57.

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 03:05:00 | `report-export` starts logging 512 MB CSV parts to `/var/lib/stockroom/exports/`, one every 12 seconds. |
| 03:09:03 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 91%` |
| 03:12:48 | Last export part logged (`part-01456.csv`), 40 writes in all. |
| 03:13:30 | `WARN disk /var/lib/stockroom at 99%` |
| 03:13:51 | Last successful api request. |
| 03:14:00 | `ERROR db: could not extend file "base/16384/2619": No space left on device` |
| 03:14:03 | `ERROR api: transaction aborted, shutting down worker pool` |
| 03:14:06 | `FATAL api: exiting (status 1)` |
| 03:16:00 – 05:28:00 | `ERROR proxy: upstream api refused connection` every 2 minutes, 67 times. |

- **No recovery:** there are no api requests after 03:13:51 and no sign of a restart in the log.
- **Other services:** `web` and `proxy` kept answering their own requests with 200s throughout, so only api-backed traffic was failing.
- **Export job's earlier history:** the first export line is already `part-01300`, so the job may have been writing before 03:05 without logging it; the log alone can't say how much it had written in total.
- **Unrelated noise:** the 43 `cache: slow command` warnings run evenly through the whole log, before and after the crash, and don't look connected.

I only read the log and the compose file; I haven't changed anything or checked the current state of the disk or the containers. Before restarting the api, space needs to be freed on `/var/lib/stockroom`, most likely by clearing the export parts, or it will fail again on the first database write.
